answers.rationale: Inline diffs are exactly what I need to feel confident about multi-file changes. Being able to see what's happening before accepting is crucial for me to trust the tool on real code.

Checkpoint rollback is a game-changer. Knowing I can undo changes if something goes wrong removes my biggest hesitation about letting an agent work autonomously. That safety net makes all the difference.
My main worry is that the agent might make subtle logic errors or introduce bugs that aren't immediately obvious. Even with diffs, catching all mistakes in a large refactor could be tricky.

answers.value: Refactoring variable names and formatting across a single module with existing test coverage
answers.rationale: I'd start with something low-risk but still useful—like renaming variables or cleaning up formatting in a well-tested module. If the agent messes up, the tests will catch it, and I can roll back. Good way to build trust gradually.
